en.title: airBaltic Signs Lufthansa Wet-Lease Deal as A220 Fleet Shrinks to 36 Aircraft
en.summary: airBaltic has signed a new wet-lease agreement with Lufthansa Group, operating up to six Airbus A220-300s with crew for Lufthansa in summer and four in winter, as it prepares to cut its A220 fleet to 36 aircraft in 2027; wet-lease flying will run alongside its own scheduled network, and its Air Serbia cooperation will continue.
body: airBaltic has signed a new wet lease agreement with Lufthansa Group in preparation to reduce its Airbus A220-300 fleet to 36 aircraft in 2027. Under the agreement, airBaltic will operate up to six Airbus A220-300s with crew for Lufthansa during the summer season and four during the winter season. Wet lease operations will form part of airBaltic's activities alongside its own scheduled network, and the new longer-term agreement will continue the existing cooperation and "enable more balanced capacity allocation in line with the airline's new business plan".

The wet-lease partnership is long-standing: in 2024, Lufthansa announced it was extending its wet lease agreement with airBaltic for three more years starting in the summer of 2025, a contract that allowed airBaltic to deploy up to 21 additional Airbus A220-300 aircraft during summer 2025 and five more aircraft during the following winter. airBaltic will also continue its wet lease cooperation with Air Serbia, with four aircraft planned for the summer season and two for the winter season. "Lufthansa Group's decision to extend our cooperation for the coming seasons reflects the trust we have built together over the past years," said Mantas Vrubliauskas, VP Network Management at airBaltic. "Our partners value airBaltic as a reliable ACMI provider, with consistent operational performance and positive feedback from both the airlines we fly for and their passengers."

The deal is part of airBaltic's financial reset. Earlier this year, airBaltic filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in the US and confirmed plans to reduce its all-Airbus A220-300 fleet from 54 aircraft to 36 before gradually returning to around 40 by 2031. In October 2026, airBaltic also confirmed that between 500 and 700 staff members could lose their jobs; the airline currently employs around 3,000 people across the Baltics. The cost-cutting measures are part of the airline's new business plan announced in August 2026, to prioritise "financial stability first, growth second".

zh.title: airBaltic與漢莎集團簽新濕租協議，A220機隊2027年縮減至36架
zh.summary: airBaltic與漢莎集團簽署新的長期濕租協議，夏季最多以6架、冬季4架空中巴士A220-300含機組為漢莎營運，配合其2027年將A220機隊縮減至36架的計畫；濕租業務將與自有定期航網並行，另與塞爾維亞航空的合作亦將延續。
body: airBaltic已與漢莎集團簽署新的濕租協議，為2027年將空中巴士A220-300機隊縮減至36架做準備。根據協議，airBaltic將在夏季最多以6架含機組的A220-300為漢莎營運，冬季則為4架；濕租營運將與airBaltic自有定期航線網絡並行。雙方表示，新簽的長期協議將延續既有合作，使運能配置更符合airBaltic新業務計畫的平衡需求。

漢莎集團與airBaltic的濕租合作行之有年：漢莎於2024年宣布將協議延長三年，自2025年夏季起生效，該合約允許airBaltic在2025年夏季部署最多21架額外A220-300，隔年冬季再增加5架。airBaltic也將延續與塞爾維亞航空的濕租合作，夏季4架、冬季2架。airBaltic網路管理副總裁Mantas Vrubliauskas表示，漢莎集團決定延續未來數季的合作，反映雙方多年建立的信任；合作夥伴肯定airBaltic是可靠的ACMI供應商，營運表現穩定，也獲得航空公司與旅客的正面回饋。
這項協議是airBaltic財務整頓的一環。該公司今年稍早已在美國申請第11章破產保護，並確認計畫將全A220-300機隊由54架縮減至36架，之後在2031年前逐步回升至約40架；2026年10月亦確認500至700名員工可能失業，目前在波羅的海地區約僱用3,000人。相關撙節措施屬於2026年8月公布的新業務計畫，優先順序為「財務穩定優先、成長其次」。
